findings.title: data_path: ADDRORDER/SAME_ADDRESS_HOST_ORDER_TAG_REUSE
findings.requirement: A request is never accepted while an older, still-unissued request of the same direction holds the same tag: in a tag-indexed write buffer the new word overwrites the old one and the old command is later issued with the new data and mask (path_07 on 2a18a7929dce, 2026-11-09: the write accepted at t=94000 to 0x160165c reached DDR at t=2929000 carrying the word and mask of the write accepted at t=2199000, 19 reuses in the run, DP-015 x17). The buffer must refuse the word (wr_data_ready low while its slot is valid) or the port must not allocate an in-flight tag; an occupancy count is not a per-slot check.

findings.title: scheduler: ADDRORDER/SAME_ADDRESS_HOST_ORDER
findings.requirement: Requests to the same word address are issued to the memory in host order: a read is never issued ahead of an older write to its address (it would return stale data), a write never ahead of an older read (the read would return the new data) or an older write (the final contents would be the older word). Reordering across DIFFERENT addresses is the scheduler's to do; same-address order is not.

Reordering across DIFFERENT addresses is the scheduler's to do; same-address order is not.

findings.title: READ issued to a bank one cycle after that bank was PRECHARGEd (no ACTIVATE between)
findings.requirement: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.expected: After PRE to bank b, no RD/WR to b until an ACT to b (JESD79-3 bank state machine).
findings.actual: PRE b=1 at cycle 183, RD b=1 at cycle 184.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 183 PRE bank 1 (A10=0), cycle 184 RD bank 1 col 0. The generated PROTO_001 tracker (row-open state from the observed ACT/PRE stream) shows bank 1 closed when the READ is issued. Never observed in simulation (no path stimulus reaches this interleaving); the scheduler or its bank_tracker gating lets a CAS follow its own precharge. Likely the same root as the open scheduler re-grant defect (commands are also held for 2-3 consecutive cycles in the trace, i.e. re-issued). [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on 2a18a7929dce]

repro.assumptions: none beyond CSR/status tie-offs; host Wishbone inputs free and, in the trace, protocol-legal

findings.title: PRECHARGE issued one cycle after a WRITE to the same bank (tWR violated; write data lost)
findings.requirement: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.expected: WR to bank b then no PRE to b for tWR (2 free cycles at 5 ns).
findings.actual: WR b=4 at cycle 173, PRE b=4 at cycle 174.
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample, 136 cycles from reset under a protocol-legal host: cycle 173 WR bank 4, cycle 174 PRE bank 4. tWR = 15 ns = 3 controller cycles, so 2 cycles must separate the last write beat from the precharge. Not observed in simulation. bank_tracker's write-recovery timer (cfg_tWR_nCK) does not gate bank_pre_allowed for the cycle after a write, or the scheduler ignores it on the row-conflict path. [found on drop 1fea117; awaiting formal re-prove on 2a18a7929dce]

repro.assumptions: none beyond CSR/status tie-offs; host Wishbone inputs free and, in the trace, protocol-legal

findings.title: Write acknowledge and read response complete in the same cycle on the one Wishbone ack line
findings.requirement: One acknowledge per accepted beat (host_interface.interface_type = wishbone_pipelined). When a write acknowledge and a read response are due in the same cycle the port must hold one of them (a one-entry response or write-ack holding register) so each completes in its own cycle.
findings.expected: One acknowledge per accepted beat (host_interface.interface_type = wishbone_pipelined). When a write acknowledge and a read response are due in the same cycle the port must hold one of them (a one-entry response or write-ack holding register) so each completes in its own cycle.
findings.actual: cex at bound 24: $past(wb_cyc_i && wb_stb_i && !wb_stall_o && wb_we_i) && rsp_valid is reachable
findings.mechanism: JasperGold counterexample 24 cycles from reset, engine L, no abstraction (cover c_HOST_001, a write beat accepted, reached at cycle 1). wb_port.sv: wr_ack_r <= wb_beat & wb_we_i (the write acknowledge, one cycle after the beat) and assign wb_ack_o = wr_ack_r | rd_ack with rd_ack = rsp_valid. A read response arriving the cycle after a write beat is accepted gives one wb_ack_o pulse for two completions; the host counts one acknowledge, waits for the other forever (a pipelined master) or mis-attributes the read data to the write (a classic one). Any legal host reaches it: issue a read, then present a write beat the cycle before the read data returns. Not seen in simulation on 2026-10-28 only because no sequence placed a write beat on that cycle (243 pipelined beats on path_07). SIMULATION WITNESS (2026-10-29, path_23_host_ack_collision, ack_collision.py): a read to an open row and a write beat accepted 41 cycles later (gap d = 40) -- the write acknowledge and the read response fall in the same cycle at t = 35.37 us; a_HOST_001 fires once, every request and response is conserved, and the host handshake stage counts 1 of 79 beats never acknowledged: the one ack pulse the two completions shared. [found on drop 99f72da45a32; awaiting formal re-prove on 2a18a7929dce]

repro.assumptions: none: host Wishbone inputs and configuration registers free
